transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for this afternoon's medication safety review of the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol, I need each of you to report any operational findings from your respective areas before I sign off on the final decision. Pharmacy, let's start with you — what are you seeing so far in terms of stocking, dispensing, or any concerns with the automated dispensing cabinets? Lab medicine, nursing education, and clinical IT, please be ready to share your findings as well. I want to make sure we have all the information on the table before we decide on any required safeguards.

transcript.text: Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. To mitigate this risk during a temporary hold, pharmacy can remove bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes.

transcript.text: From the laboratory medicine perspective, I need to flag a critical operational finding. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this anticoagulant protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. This means we won't have anti-Xa-level monitoring available for the night shift or the remainder of this week, and any safeguards should account for the aPTT-based monitoring schedule.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From the nursing education perspective, I have a critical finding. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Under our current policy, each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they can administer this medication. Morgan, this is something we need to account for in any safeguards you decide on this afternoon.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: From the clinical IT perspective, I can confirm that a high-priority electronic medication-record alert is ready to be deployed at 16:00 today. This alert will warn clinicians about concentration selection — specifically the 1 mg/mL versus 2 mg/mL issue Leah identified — and will require acknowledgment before the order can be released. This can serve as an additional safeguard alongside the pharmacy and nursing measures already discussed.
transcript.speaker: A5

Use aPTT every six hours as the approved replacement monitoring method until the anti-Xa analyzer is calibrated and available after Friday at 17:00.
Ensure charge-nurse sign-off is obtained for each of the 18 non-credentialed nurses on tonight's shift before they administer the anticoagulant.
Deploy the concentration-selection electronic alert at 16:00 today with mandatory acknowledgment before order release.
